title: Birdwatching boom
paragraphs: Many young Brits are buying binoculars in hopes of encountering one of nature's most physically and audibly beautiful creatures - birds. You might think of birdwatching as an old-fashioned pastime most often enjoyed by the generations before you, but surveys conducted by the RSPB show a 47% increase in participation overall, with an even higher 1,088% surge by Gen Zers. So, why do so many young people want to flock to the park to watch birds?

A group leader at RSPB Bristol highlighted how many students have joined his outings. He mentioned that some who join have 'never been out in their local nature spaces' and 'want to explore'. He added that the diversity of species you can find is impressive 'considering it's so urban' around the city. There is also the rise of a desire to disconnect from technology and go outside, or as Gen Z would call it touch grass, to help with mental health. Research from the University of Surrey has looked at how bird sounds restore attention and even alleviate stress.

Ironically, when interviewed by BBC Bristol, individuals mentioned how phones and social media have actually helped encourage the hype of this hobby. There are now a variety of apps in which you can record a birdsong and have it instantly identified. People also use social media to share knowledge and location for birds. A phenomenon known as 'bioblitzing', a combination of bio and blitzing, has emerged. This is when a walker documents as many birds and other species of animals as they can within a limited amount of time. It has been said to create a safe space in which birdwatchers can get into friendly competitions over who can spot the most! Furthermore, a buzz around the birdwatching hashtag has cultivated humour around turning 30 and entering your 'birdwatching era'.

Whether it's the chance to reconnect with nature, improve mental wellbeing, or join a growing online community, birdwatching is no longer seen as a hobby reserved for older generations. Young people are embracing it in record numbers, using both technology and the outdoors to discover the wildlife on their doorstep. From identifying birdsongs with apps to competing in bioblitzing challenges, a modern twist has transformed the pastime into something fresh and accessible. It seems that for Gen Z and young millennials alike, birdwatching has become a hoot.
chineseParagraphs: 许多英国年轻人正在购买双筒望远镜，希望邂逅自然界中外观和声音最美丽的生物之一——鸟类。你可能认为观鸟是一种过时的消遣，通常由老一辈人喜爱，但英国皇家鸟类保护协会进行的调查显示，总体参与率增加了47%，而Z世代的参与率更是激增了1088%。那么，为什么这么多年轻人想要成群结队地去公园观鸟呢？
英国皇家鸟类保护协会布里斯托尔分会的一位组长强调了有多少学生加入了他的郊游活动。他提到，一些参加者“从未去过他们当地的野外空间”，并且“想要探索”。他补充说，考虑到城市周围“如此城市化”，你能找到的物种多样性令人印象深刻。此外，人们也越来越渴望摆脱科技，走到户外，或者用Z世代的话说“接触大自然”，以改善心理健康。萨里大学的研究关注了鸟鸣如何恢复注意力甚至减轻压力。

讽刺的是，在接受BBC布里斯托尔频道采访时，人们提到手机和社交媒体实际上助长了这项爱好的热潮。现在有各种各样的应用程序，你可以录制鸟鸣声并立即得到识别。人们还使用社交媒体分享关于鸟类的知识和位置信息。一种被称为“生物闪电战”的现象出现了，它是“生物”和“闪电战”的组合。这是指徒步者在有限时间内尽可能多地记录鸟类和其他动物物种。据说这创造了一个安全的空间，观鸟者可以展开友好的竞赛，看谁能发现最多的鸟类！此外，围绕观鸟话题标签的热议也营造了关于年过三十、进入“观鸟时代”的幽默氛围。
无论是为了重新与自然建立联系、改善心理健康，还是加入一个不断壮大的在线社区，观鸟都不再被视为老一辈人的专属爱好。年轻人正以前所未有的数量欣然接受它，利用科技和户外活动来发现自家门前的野生动物。从用应用程序识别鸟鸣，到参与生物闪电战挑战，现代元素的融入将这项消遣转变为新鲜且易于参与的活动。看来，对于Z世代和年轻的千禧一代来说，观鸟已经变成了一件非常有趣的事。

vocabulary.entry: binoculars /bɪˈnɒkjələz/ n. 双筒望远镜（复数）

vocabulary.translation: 她用双筒望远镜观鸟。

vocabulary.entry: encounter /ɪnˈkaʊntə(r)/ v. 偶然碰到，遭遇（书面语）
vocabulary.example: I encountered an old friend on the train.
vocabulary.translation: 我在火车上偶然遇到了一位老朋友。

vocabulary.entry: audibly /ˈɔːdəbli/ adv. 可听见地（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The birds were audibly singing in the trees.
vocabulary.translation: 鸟儿在树上歌声可闻。

vocabulary.entry: birdwatching /ˈbɜːdwɒtʃɪŋ/ n. 观鸟（活动）
vocabulary.example: Birdwatching is a popular hobby in the UK.
vocabulary.translation: 观鸟在英国是一项受欢迎的爱好。

vocabulary.entry: old-fashioned /ˌəʊld ˈfæʃnd/ adj. 过时的，老式的
vocabulary.example: He has an old-fashioned view of marriage.
vocabulary.translation: 他对婚姻有过时的看法。

vocabulary.entry: pastime /ˈpɑːstaɪm/ n. 消遣，娱乐活动（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Reading is a popular pastime for many people.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读是许多人的一种流行消遣。

vocabulary.entry: surge /sɜːdʒ/ n. 激增，急剧上升（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There has been a surge in demand for electric cars.
vocabulary.translation: 对电动汽车的需求激增。

vocabulary.entry: flock /flɒk/ v. 聚集，成群结队（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Tourists flock to the city every summer.
vocabulary.translation: 每年夏天游客成群结队地涌向这座城市。

vocabulary.entry: outing /ˈaʊtɪŋ/ n. 短途旅行，郊游
vocabulary.example: We went on a family outing to the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 我们全家去海滩郊游。

vocabulary.entry: diversity /daɪˈvɜːsəti/ n. 多样性，多样化（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There is a wide diversity of opinion on this issue.
vocabulary.translation: 关于这个问题存在广泛多样的意见。

vocabulary.entry: urban /ˈɜːbən/ adj. 城市的，都市的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Crime is a major problem in many urban areas.
vocabulary.translation: 犯罪是许多城市地区的主要问题。

vocabulary.definition: 接触大自然，回到现实（网络用语）
vocabulary.entry: touch grass /ˌtʌtʃ ˈɡrɑːs/ phr. 接触大自然，回到现实（网络用语）
vocabulary.example: If you're feeling stressed, you should go outside and touch grass.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你感到压力大，你应该出去接触一下大自然。

vocabulary.entry: restore /rɪˈstɔː(r)/ v. 恢复，修复（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The doctor's treatment restored her health.
vocabulary.translation: 医生的治疗恢复了她的健康。

vocabulary.entry: alleviate /əˈliːvieɪt/ v. 减轻，缓解（书面语）
vocabulary.example: This medicine should alleviate your symptoms.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药应该能缓解你的症状。

vocabulary.definition: 讽刺地，具有讽刺意味的是
vocabulary.entry: ironically /aɪˈrɒnɪkli/ adv. 讽刺地，具有讽刺意味的是
vocabulary.example: Ironically, he got the job despite having no experience.
vocabulary.translation: 讽刺的是，他尽管没有经验却得到了这份工作。

vocabulary.entry: hype /haɪp/ n. 大肆宣传，炒作（口语）
vocabulary.example: The film lived up to all the hype.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影不负所有的炒作。

vocabulary.entry: phenomenon /fəˈnɒmɪnən/ n. 现象（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The phenomenon of global warming is well documented.
vocabulary.translation: 全球变暖这一现象已有详细记录。

vocabulary.definition: 生物闪电战（生态学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: bioblitzing /ˈbaɪəʊˌblɪtsɪŋ/ n. 生物闪电战（生态学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Bioblitzing is a fun way to document local wildlife.
vocabulary.translation: 生物闪电战是记录当地野生动物的有趣方式。

vocabulary.entry: document /ˈdɒkjument/ v. 记录，记载（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film documents the effects of climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影记录了气候变化的影响。

vocabulary.definition: 话题标签（社交媒体术语）
vocabulary.entry: hashtag /ˈhæʃtæɡ/ n. 话题标签（社交媒体术语）
vocabulary.example: The hashtag #birdwatching was trending on social media.
vocabulary.translation: #birdwatching这个标签在社交媒体上很热门。

vocabulary.entry: cultivate /ˈkʌltɪveɪt/ v. 培养，培育（书面语）
vocabulary.example: It's important to cultivate good relationships with colleagues.
vocabulary.translation: 与同事培养良好的关系很重要。

vocabulary.definition: 重新连接，重新建立联系
vocabulary.entry: reconnect /ˌriːkəˈnekt/ v. 重新连接，重新建立联系
vocabulary.example: After years apart, they reconnected through social media.
vocabulary.translation: 分开多年后，他们通过社交媒体重新取得了联系。

vocabulary.entry: reserved for /rɪˈzɜːvd fɔː(r)/ phr. 为……保留，专供（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The front row is reserved for VIPs.
vocabulary.translation: 前排是为VIP预留的。

vocabulary.entry: embrace /ɪmˈbreɪs/ v. 欣然接受，拥抱（书面语）
vocabulary.example: It's time to embrace new technology.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候欣然接受新技术了。

vocabulary.definition: 创纪录的数量（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: record numbers /ˈrekɔːd ˈnʌmbəz/ phr. 创纪录的数量（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Tourists visited the city in record numbers last year.
vocabulary.translation: 去年创纪录数量的游客访问了这座城市。

vocabulary.entry: doorstep /ˈdɔːstep/ n. 门阶，家门口（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: There is a park on our doorstep.
vocabulary.translation: 我们家门口就有一个公园。

vocabulary.entry: twist /twɪst/ n. 转折，变化
vocabulary.example: The story had an unexpected twist at the end.
vocabulary.translation: 故事结尾有一个意想不到的转折。

vocabulary.definition: 有趣的人或事，开心的时刻（口语）
vocabulary.entry: hoot /huːt/ n. 有趣的人或事，开心的时刻（口语）
vocabulary.example: The party was a real hoot.
vocabulary.translation: 这个派对真的很好玩。
